title: GraphQL API Developer
description: Design flexible, high-performance schema-driven APIs, federated enterprise graphs, and efficient client data-fetching layers.

goal.objective: Architect unified enterprise GraphQL schemas that eliminate over-fetching, power multi-client applications, and unify backend microservices.

learn.summary: Master GraphQL Schema Definition Language (SDL), query resolvers, mutations, subscriptions, Apollo Server/Client, DataLoader caching, and enterprise Apollo Federation.
prerequisites: Node.js, Go, or Python backend basics

capstone_projects.title: Enterprise Federated GraphQL Supergraph with Apollo Federation v2
capstone_projects.description: Architect a distributed GraphQL supergraph uniting inventory, user, and billing subgraphs with entity interfaces, subgraph composition checks, and schema contracts.

capstone_projects.title: Real-Time Collaborative GraphQL API with Subscriptions & DataLoader
capstone_projects.description: Build a high-performance GraphQL API featuring real-time WebSocket subscriptions, query complexity analysis, and strict DataLoader batching to eliminate N+1 queries.

interview_focus: GraphQL N+1 Query Problem & DataLoader Batching/Caching Mechanics
Apollo Federation Architecture (Entities, Keys, External Fields, Query Plan Generation)
Schema Design Best Practices (Relay Connection Specification, Input Object Unions)
Security & DoS Protection (Query Depth Limiting, Complexity Cost Analysis, Introspection Control)
GraphQL Over HTTP vs WebSockets vs Server-Sent Events (SSE) for Subscriptions

tree.name: GraphQL Fundamentals & Ecosystem
tree.description: Master GraphQL fundamentals: Schema-driven architecture, precise client data fetching, eliminating over/under-fetching, and understanding the GraphQL specification.

children.name: Core Concepts: Queries, Mutations, Subscriptions
children.description: Master core GraphQL operations: Read queries, write mutations, real-time reactive subscriptions, field arguments, aliases, and reusable fragments.

resources.title: Exploring GraphQL Queries, Mutations, and Subscriptions (LogRocket)

children.name: Schema Definition Language (SDL) & Core Type System
children.description: Design schemas with Schema Definition Language (SDL): Scalar types (String, Int, Float, Boolean, ID, custom scalars), Object types, Enums, Interfaces, Unions, and Input types.

resources.title: Introduction to GraphQL Schema Definition Language (Howtographql.com)

children.name: GraphQL Directives
children.description: Leverage built-in and custom schema directives: `@include`, `@skip`, `@deprecated`, and authoring custom schema transformation directives (e.g. `@auth`, `@cacheControl`).

resources.title: End-To-End Type-Safety with GraphQL, Prisma & React: Codegen & Deployment (Prisma)

children.name: GraphQL vs. REST: Understanding the Trade-offs
children.description: Evaluate architectural tradeoffs: GraphQL vs REST vs gRPC regarding network roundtrips, schema contracts, caching simplicity, CDN edge caching, and attack surfaces.

resources.title: GraphQL vs. REST: A Definitive Guide (Apigee)

children.name: GraphQL Tooling & Environment Setup
children.description: Set up modern GraphQL development environments: Apollo Sandbox, GraphiQL IDE, GraphQL Playground, ESLint GraphQL plugins, and Prettier schema formatting.

resources.title: Exploring your GraphQL API with Apollo Studio

tree.name: GraphQL Server Implementation
tree.description: Implement robust GraphQL servers: Request execution lifecycles, AST query parsing, validation against schema, resolver execution phases, and response serialization.

resources.title: Building a GraphQL API with Node.js and Apollo Server (Dev.to)

children.name: Choosing & Setting Up a GraphQL Server Framework
children.description: Deploy modern GraphQL server frameworks: Apollo Server, Yoga (Envelop), Mercurius for Fastify, NestJS GraphQL module, and Express GraphQL.

resources.title: Get Started with Apollo Server in Node.js
Building a GraphQL API with Express.js and GraphQL.js
End-To-End Type-Safety with GraphQL, Prisma & React: Codegen & Deployment (Prisma)

children.name: Schema-First vs. Code-First Development
children.description: Evaluate schema design methodologies: Schema-first development (SDL-driven with codegen) vs Code-first / Type-first development with TypeGraphQL, Pothos, or Nexus.

resources.title: GraphQL Schema Design: Code-First vs. Schema-First (LogRocket)

children.name: Resolvers: Data Fetching & Transformation
children.description: Implement resolver functions: Resolving parent arguments, field parameters, contextual request state, and abstract AST info objects.

children.name: Context, Middleware & Plugins
children.description: Inject request-scoped context: User authentication tokens, database connection pools, DataLoader instances, and middleware pipelines using GraphQL Envelop.

children.name: Connecting to Various Data Sources (DBs, REST, Microservices)
children.description: Connect heterogeneous data sources: Relational databases via Prisma/Drizzle ORM, NoSQL stores, internal microservices via REST connectors, and third-party APIs.

resources.title: Building a GraphQL API on Top of REST APIs (Apollo Blog)
End-To-End Type-Safety with GraphQL, Prisma & React: Codegen & Deployment (Prisma)

children.name: Input Validation & Sanitization
children.description: Enforce strict input validation: Validating mutation input types with Zod, Joi, or custom scalar constraints, sanitizing strings against XSS, and handling invalid arguments.

resources.title: GraphQL Input Validation with Joi (The Guild)

children.name: Error Handling & Custom Errors
children.description: Standardize GraphQL error formatting: RFC-compliant errors array, custom extension codes (`UNAUTHENTICATED`, `FORBIDDEN`, `BAD_USER_INPUT`), and masking internal server errors in production.

children.name: Subscriptions for Real-time Data
children.description: Implement real-time GraphQL subscriptions: WebSockets protocol (`graphql-ws`), Server-Sent Events (SSE), Redis Pub/Sub backends for horizontal cluster scaling.

resources.title: Implementing GraphQL Subscriptions with Apollo Server (LogRocket)

tree.name: Enhancing GraphQL APIs
tree.description: Harden and optimize GraphQL APIs: Solving the N+1 query problem, client-side/server-side caching, and query performance tuning.

resources.title: End-To-End Type-Safety with GraphQL, Prisma & React: Codegen & Deployment (Prisma)

children.name: Authentication & Authorization in GraphQL
children.description: Implement granular authentication and authorization: Role-based access control (RBAC), attribute-based access control (ABAC) at schema, field, and object resolver levels.

resources.title: GraphQL Authorization with OIDC and OpenFGA (Auth0)

children.name: Caching Strategies (Client, Server, CDN)
children.description: Implement multi-tier caching: Full-query HTTP caching with GET requests, `@cacheControl` directives, Apollo Server response caching, and CDN edge caching.

children.name: Solving the N+1 Problem with DataLoader
children.description: Eliminate the N+1 problem using DataLoader: Batching database queries across concurrent resolver executions, request-scoped memoization caching, and prime keys.

resources.title: Optimizing GraphQL Performance with DataLoader (Apollo Blog)

children.name: Persisted Queries & Query Batching
children.description: Implement Automatic Persisted Queries (APQ): Sending SHA256 query hashes instead of verbose query strings, reducing request payload size and enabling CDN caching.

resources.title: End-To-End Type-Safety with GraphQL, Prisma & React: Codegen & Deployment (Prisma)

children.name: Pagination, Filtering, and Sorting
children.description: Implement standardized pagination: Relay Connection specification (Cursor-based pagination with `edges`, `node`, `pageInfo`, `hasNextPage`), sorting, and multi-criteria filtering.

children.name: Handling File Uploads
children.description: Handle file uploads in GraphQL: Multipart request specification (`graphql-multipart-request-spec`), Apollo Upload Server, or pre-signed S3 upload URL patterns.

resources.title: File Uploads with Apollo Server (Apollo Docs)

tree.name: Advanced GraphQL Architectures
tree.description: Architect enterprise GraphQL topologies: Federated microservice graphs, distributed schema stitching, and serverless edge deployments.

resources.title: Building a GraphQL API with Lambda & Apollo Server (Serverless.com)

children.name: GraphQL Federation & Schema Stitching
children.description: Build enterprise federated graphs using Apollo Federation 2: Composing subgraphs into a unified supergraph with `@key`, `@shareable`, `@external`, and Apollo Router.

resources.title: Microservices with GraphQL Federation (Netflix Open Source)
End-To-End Type-Safety with GraphQL, Prisma & React: Codegen & Deployment (Prisma)

children.name: Serverless GraphQL
children.description: Deploy serverless GraphQL: Hosting Apollo Server / Yoga on AWS Lambda, Cloudflare Workers, or Vercel Edge with connection-pooled databases (Prisma Accelerate / Neon).

resources.title: Serverless GraphQL with Apollo Server Lambda (Apollo Blog)
Building a Serverless GraphQL API with AWS AppSync

children.name: GraphQL API Gateways & Proxies
children.description: Deploy high-performance GraphQL gateways: Apollo Router (written in Rust), GraphQL Hive gateway, and Envoy GraphQL filters for low-latency query planning and execution.

resources.title: The Evolution of API Gateways to GraphQL (Kong)

tree.name: Operationalizing GraphQL APIs
tree.description: Operationalize GraphQL in production: Automated testing, monitoring, security controls, and continuous integration.

resources.title: Continuous Integration and Deployment for GraphQL (The Guild)

children.name: Testing GraphQL APIs
children.description: Test GraphQL APIs systematically: Unit testing resolver functions, integration testing operations with Apollo Server test harnesses, and end-to-end Supertest assertion suites.

resources.title: Automated Testing for GraphQL APIs (Apollo Blog)
End-To-End Type-Safety with GraphQL, Prisma & React: Codegen & Deployment (Prisma)

children.name: Monitoring, Logging & Tracing
children.description: Monitor GraphQL performance: Distributed tracing with OpenTelemetry, field-level execution latency metrics with Apollo Studio or GraphQL Hive, and logging slow queries.

children.name: Advanced Security: Rate Limiting, Depth Limiting, Query Cost Analysis
children.description: Protect GraphQL against DoS: Enforcing maximum query depth limits (`graphql-depth-limit`), query complexity/cost analysis, and distributed IP/user rate limiting.

resources.title: GraphQL Security: Preventing DOS Attacks (Apollo Blog)

children.name: Deployment & CI/CD for GraphQL
children.description: Automate GraphQL deployment: Continuous integration checking schema changes, validating supergraph composition, and zero-downtime rolling gateway deployments.

resources.title: Deploying a GraphQL API to AWS with Serverless Framework (Serverless.com)

children.name: Schema Evolution & Versioning
children.description: Evolve GraphQL schemas without breaking changes: Deprecating fields gracefully with `@deprecated(reason: "...")`, adding nullable fields, and avoiding enum value removals.

resources.title: End-To-End Type-Safety with GraphQL, Prisma & React: Codegen & Deployment (Prisma)

children.name: Schema Registry & Automated Schema Checks
children.description: Implement schema registries: Using Apollo Studio or GraphQL Hive to enforce schema checks, detect breaking changes on PRs, and track client operation adoption.

resources.title: GraphQL Inspector for Schema Checks (The Guild)
Managing Your GraphQL Schema with a Registry (Chasemoskal)

tree.name: GraphQL Client Integration
tree.description: Integrate modern GraphQL clients: Caching normalized data, optimistic UI mutations, and end-to-end type safety.

resources.title: Getting Started with GraphQL on the Client (Howtographql.com)

children.name: Choosing a GraphQL Client (Apollo Client, Relay, Urql)
children.description: Select the right frontend client: Comparing Apollo Client, Relay for performance-critical Facebook-scale apps, and Urql for lightweight modular flexibility.

children.name: Consuming GraphQL APIs (Queries, Mutations, Subscriptions)
children.description: Execute client operations: Utilizing `useQuery`, `useMutation`, and `useSubscription` React hooks with loading, error, and data state handling.

resources.title: Queries, Mutations, and Subscriptions (Apollo Client Docs)
End-To-End Type-Safety with GraphQL, Prisma & React: Codegen & Deployment (Prisma)

children.name: Client-side Caching & State Management
children.description: Master normalized client caching: InMemoryCache configuration, custom `TypePolicies`, field key arguments, merge functions, and local state management.

children.name: Optimistic UI Updates
children.description: Implement optimistic UI updates: Specifying `optimisticResponse` in mutations to update client cache instantly before server confirmation, with automated rollback on error.

children.name: Client-side Error Handling & UI Feedback
children.description: Handle client errors gracefully: Differentiating network errors from GraphQL execution errors, toast notification triggers, and token refresh retry links.

resources.title: Handling GraphQL Errors on the Client (LogRocket)

children.name: Client-side File Uploads
children.description: Implement client file uploads: Using `apollo-upload-client` to stream files via GraphQL multipart requests or coordinating S3 presigned URL uploads.

resources.title: End-To-End Type-Safety with GraphQL, Prisma & React: Codegen & Deployment (Prisma)

children.name: Code Generation from Schema (GraphQL Code Generator)
children.description: Generate type-safe frontend code using GraphQL Code Generator: Compiling schema and `.graphql` documents into fully typed React hooks, TypeScript types, and SDKs.

resources.title: Generating React Hooks from GraphQL Operations (The Guild)
Apollo Client with TypeScript & CodeGen (Apollo Blog)

tree.name: Project & Career Readiness
tree.description: Build a demonstrable GraphQL portfolio: Architecting end-to-end full-stack applications, documenting schema designs, and preparing for GraphQL technical interviews.

resources.title: How to Build a Portfolio Website (freeCodeCamp.org)

children.name: Building a Production-Ready GraphQL API Project
children.description: Build an enterprise GraphQL capstone: Federated supergraph with Apollo Router, PostgreSQL backend with DataLoader, Apollo Client frontend with codegen, and CI breaking change checks.

children.name: Portfolio Development & Interview Preparation
children.description: Master GraphQL technical interviews: Explain query execution lifecycle, derive DataLoader batching mechanics, design federated enterprise schemas, and solve query cost defense problems.

resources.title: How to Create an Awesome Portfolio (freeCodeCamp.org)
End-To-End Type-Safety with GraphQL, Prisma & React: Codegen & Deployment (Prisma)
